title: Scammy subscription model but somewhat useful app
body:
Considering who this app is aimed at, I find it very scammy to make unsubscribing so unnecessarily difficult. You cannot simply do it in the App Store like with all other apps. They make you pay for 3 months at a time as well. I find it difficult to deal with admin. As do many others with ADHD. When things like this are difficult, I tend to give up. 

The app itself is not bad but everything takes ages in it. It’s pretty but I’d prefer it to be less graphics and more straight up useful. Graphics could still be used without taking so unnecessary long time to play out. The Deep Work feature is very calming but also very annoying if you are pulled away from it (which as a mum to a toddler happens pretty often). If you close the app, the timer restarts completely. You cannot pause the music with your headphones so have to get your phone to do it which can be another distraction. 

I haven’t tried everything in it yet, and only using it at this point because I’m paying for it. As soon as I figure out how to unsubscribe, I will.

title: Perfectly designed scam for ADHD
body: This company is a perfectly designed con. It's app 'Clarify' is terrible for people with ADHD which is its whole selling point. I tried it on a free subscription and lasted literally 2 days before realising it was a complete waste of time and deleted it. They then charged me £30.99 in December, February and April and I didnt notice until I got notifications that they had been declined this month. Thats when I noticed all of these charges. I checked my emails and they hadn't sent a single invoice or warning for any of these charges. It's like they market towards people with ADHD, knowing they are unlikely to notice or remember it turns into a payed subscription. They then dont send emails hoping you forget and didn't let me subscribe through the App Store where most people with adhd know to check their subscriptions. It's a crazy targeted scam. I wouldn't touch any of their apps or give them any access to payment details. Two days of having this app downloaded cost me nearly £100 without me noticing.

title: So far it’s good
body:
The app has been helpful so far. It’s nice to have kind of a central point to keep going back to when I feel stuck or overwhelmed. I like the “Deep Work” time, the music is really relaxing and the timer reminds me there is an end to the work!
The overall layout is OK. The illustrations are really beautiful too.

My one gripe with the app is how frustrating and overwhelming all the marketing is for someone with ADHD. Before I had even logged in (to an app that is made to help me focus) I had been asked so many questions, shown four different screens full of options, given ten different “add ons” commercials, and been given the choice of paying three different amounts for what should be a free trial. (“How much do you think this is worth?”, “Do you want the food app?” “Do you want the reading app?” “Do you want additional information things or just the Clarify option?”aghhh!!) Considering it’s a paid app (and quite expensive) I would rather they keep in mind WHY I need the app and not completely overwhelm me with a hundred different options!! Also, once logged in it keeps pushing them. Maybe just forget the initial push and have them there in the app to appeal to people instead. Just keep it simple.

If you are genuinely trying to manage ADHD, you’d be far better off reading a reputable book on the subject, seeking proper coping strategies, or talking to a professional. In fact, the app may be counterproductive: spending more time on a screen can make symptoms worse, not better. Overall, very disappointing - avoid at all costs.

title: Be warned… it’s VERY difficult to cancel a subscription!
body:
I signed up for a free trial on the app to help me focus on some assignments I need to do. The Deep Work room was great, it really helped me. 

BUT I couldn’t remember what date I had to cancel by, to avoid being charged. I went into my App Store subscriptions, only to find it wasn’t on there. Tried to look on the app, but it kept saying I needed to ‘sign in’ - I couldn’t remember how I’d signed in the first place (google/FB/email etc).

Anyway, I got distracted by something and thought no more about it. I’m sure this is what they hope will happen, as they’re targeting people with ADHD. 

A few days later, my online banking informed me that Fabulous had taken £30.99 from my account.  

Went onto the app again. Eventually I found a button that said ‘Manage my subscription’… but that just told me I needed to go to a website outside of the app - it didn’t automatically redirect me. I had to go onto safari and TYPE the web address in, as I couldn’t copy and paste it. Logged in with email, which thankfully worked. And from there I could cancel my subscription. Interestingly, before it let me cancel, it tried to offer me other financial options. For example, I could get 20% off the subscription price and only have to pay £1.79 a month.

?????

How could it go from being £30.99 for 2 months, to £1.79 per month? Had they automatically put me on the most expensive, premium subscription when I signed up for the free trial? Why would I want that? 

I wish I’d read the reviews first. I agree with other comments; this app is exploitative.
author: JJLittleMixTheScript

title: Urgh!  Run away!!!
body:
I lasted 3 days with this app. 

The first red flag really should have been the constant begging for money.  Donations to the app developers, nominal fees and then not one but two subscriptions?!!!*  

The second was the Sudo-therapeutic, patronising, computerised American accent.  It went through me like nails on a chalk board. 

This app is not intuitive in anyway and seems purposely complicated.  I hate hate hated it. It irritated me more than any other app I’ve used. 
The app doesn’t need to go back to the drawing board, the drawing board needs burning and the ashes launched into space… Although, space has many stars, this deserves none.  I’m astounded it managed a 4.1 rating. 

*it doesn’t tell you about the two subscriptions until you try to cancel, which you can’t do through the app.  I had one for Fabulous and one for Clarity ADHD.  Both looking to take £30 odd out my account.  You only realise this when you log in via a web browser and you’re told you have two accounts, which would you like to log into.  Both have a subscription attached which need cancelling separately.

title: ADHD Tax strikes again
body:
So I’ve been a user of the main Fabulous app for a few years now. I’m inconsistent because of ADHD but I always come back. 

I love the app. I recently redownloaded and was pleasantly surprised to see that they’ve reduced the price of premium to something I could actually afford, I think around £20. Bonus! 

Only to discover there’s now an ADHD friendly app! Sold! I immediately downloaded it. I deleted it within 10 minutes.  

First, there’s the immediate ableist assertion that ADHD is a superpower. F off.

From the little I could see, it’s just the same old regular Fabulous app, repackaged to look like it supports ADHD brains better.

I have no idea if it does, because there doesn’t seem to be an option to use a free version of the app like there is with Fabulous.

I couldn’t get past the “free trial, £40 a year” screen. So not only are you REQUIRED to pay if you want to ADHD version, it’s double the normal version. 

And let’s be honest, no ADHD person is going to remember to cancel their free subscription. 

Honestly this app feels like it’s doing more to advantage of ADHD folks who are susceptible to impulse purchases and make things LESS accessible/more expensive to us than it is to neurotypical counterparts. 

I’d like to hope this is just them trying to get the app off the ground and won’t be forever but let’s just wait and see.

Oh, and the MAIN REASON I deleted it instead of holding on for a while? There’s a notification which I can’t get rid of because of the paywall 😭
